about: What a visitor does with the Atari 2600 on its page at 6502.dbhq.uk: nothing to load, press Start, and play the bundled game, 2048 2600, by Carlos Duarte do Nascimento (Chester), under the MIT licence (machines/atari-2600/cartridges/2048/README.md). The page renders these steps and the controls. The controls are the console's joysticks and switches; the keys and the gamepad buttons that work them are the page's own map, shown beside it. Atari2600AcceptanceTests boots the same file and checks its picture against machines/atari-2600/expected-frames.json, which the browser check also reads.
author: Carlos Duarte do Nascimento (Chester)
credit: 2048 2600 is by Carlos Duarte do Nascimento (Chester), with PAL support by SvOlli and a fix by Ben Combee, under the MIT licence. It is a port of 2048 by Gabriele Cirulli. The cartridge art, by Jenn Harrison, is not part of the game and is not shown here.

steps.says: The machine switches on with 2048 2600 in it. Its title shows the tiles 2, 0, 4, 8 and 2, 6, 0, 0 in two rows, their colours changing every frame, with his handle, CHEST over ERBR, under them.
A one-player game starts: a grey board of four by four cells with one 2 tile on it, and the score, at zero, above it.

steps.do: Push the joystick up, down, left or right.
steps.says: Every tile slides as far as it can that way, two tiles of the same value that meet join into one of twice the value, and a new tile appears. The game ends when no move is left.

steps.do: On the title, press the right fire button, or press GAME SELECT.
steps.says: The right fire button starts a two-player game, in which the players take turns on one board. GAME SELECT switches between the one-player and the two-player game, and the game it chooses starts at once.

steps.do: If the page is set to PAL, flip the colour switch to black and white.
steps.says: The game makes PAL frames only with the switch at black and white, as its author's README says; at colour it makes NTSC frames.

controls.does: shifts every tile on the board one way
on the title, starts a one-player game; when a game is over, starts it again
on the title, starts a two-player game; when a game is over, starts it again
switches between the one-player and the two-player game, which starts at once
at black and white the game makes PAL frames, and at colour NTSC frames
